# Lock Support

`LockSupport` supplies low-level thread parking and unparking for building
synchronisation utilities. A thread can park while a condition is false rather
than repeatedly checking it; another thread can unpark it when the condition may
have changed. The condition and the coordination protocol still need to be
managed separately.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this example, attendees can:

- explain the single permit associated with a thread and why an `unpark()`
  before `park()` can avoid a missed signal;
- explain why a parked thread must recheck its condition and why parking does
  not provide mutual exclusion; and
- identify the monitor’s happens-before relationship and the limitations of this
  illustrative queue protocol.

## Prerequisite

Install an
[Oracle Java 8](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java8) JDK
or newer and ensure `java` and `javac` resolve to it in the terminal running
this example.

## The program to inspect

A bounded queue must wait when full or empty. `SharedQueue` checks the condition
and registers a waiter inside the same `synchronized` block, then releases the
monitor before parking. A producer or consumer changing the queue selects and
unparks a registered thread while holding that monitor. Parking while holding a
lock does not release it and can deadlock if the thread needed to make progress
requires the same lock.

`unpark()` makes at most one permit available to its target; permits do not
accumulate. If an already started waiter is unparked before its intended
`park()`, that call can consume the permit and return without blocking. This
depends on no intervening park consuming the permit: the logging between
registration and parking can itself involve blocking, so the example is not a
proof of a generally reliable signalling protocol. The API warns that
intermediary uses of `park()` can interfere.

`park()` may also return because the thread is interrupted or spuriously. The
loop therefore rechecks the condition under the monitor; being unparked does not
reserve an item or a space. These methods do not implement cancellation: they do
not clear or handle interrupt status, so an interrupted waiter can repeatedly
return from `park()` and retry. No fairness or bounded waiting is guaranteed.

The queue’s monitor provides mutual exclusion for the condition checks and
updates. Under the JMM, unlocking that monitor happens before a subsequent lock
of the same monitor, providing visibility and ordering for those accesses.
Parking and unparking alone do not make queue operations atomic or protect
shared state. The separate concurrent queues track waiters; `isEmpty()` itself
is not synchronised and should not be used concurrently with queue updates.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.Queue;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentLinkedQueue;
import java.util.concurrent.locks.LockSupport;

import static demo.utils.Logs.log;
import static demo.utils.Numbers.requireGreaterThanZero;

public final class SharedQueue {

    private final Queue<Integer> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    private final int capacity;

    /* Thread-safe queues for tracking blocked threads */
    private final Queue<Thread> waitingProducers = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>();
    private final Queue<Thread> waitingConsumers = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>();

    public SharedQueue(final int capacity) {
        this.capacity = requireGreaterThanZero(capacity);
    }

    public void produce(final int value) {
        while (true) {
            synchronized (this) {
                /* These two operations (`queue.size() < capacity` and `queue.offer(value)`) need to be done
                    atomically, otherwise there may be a race condition and two or more threads may be able to add
                    elements together, exceeding the queue capacity. */
                if (queue.size() < capacity) {
                    queue.offer(value);
                    log("Produced: " + value + " (size: " + queue.size() + ')');
                    unparkNextWaitingConsumer();
                    return;
                }

                /* Register while holding the queue lock. This prevents a consumer from freeing space and missing this
                    producer between the full-queue check and registration. */
                waitingProducers.add(Thread.currentThread());
            }

            log("Queue is full. Producer is waiting...");
            LockSupport.park(); /* Wait until space is available */
            waitingProducers.remove(Thread.currentThread());
        }
    }

    public int consume() {
        while (true) {
            synchronized (this) {
                /* These two operations (`queue.isEmpty()` and `queue.poll()`) need to be done atomically, otherwise
                    there may be a race condition and two or more threads may be able to poll elements at the same
                    time, even when there are no more elements available.*/
                if (!queue.isEmpty()) {
                    final int value = queue.poll();
                    log("Consumed: " + value + " (size: " + queue.size() + ')');
                    unparkNextWaitingProducer();
                    return value;
                }

                /* Register while holding the queue lock. This prevents a producer from adding an item and missing this
                    consumer between the empty-queue check and registration. */
                waitingConsumers.add(Thread.currentThread());
            }

            log("Queue is empty. Consumer is waiting...");
            LockSupport.park(); /* Wait until an item is available */
            waitingConsumers.remove(Thread.currentThread());
        }
    }

    private void unparkNextWaitingConsumer() {
        final Thread thread = waitingConsumers.poll();
        if (thread != null) {
            LockSupport.unpark(thread);
        }
    }

    private void unparkNextWaitingProducer() {
        final Thread thread = waitingProducers.poll();
        if (thread != null) {
            LockSupport.unpark(thread);
        }
    }

    public int capacity() {
        return capacity;
    }

    public boolean isEmpty() {
        return queue.isEmpty();
    }
}
```

The helper encapsulates waiter registration, parking, and unparking. It does not
replace the queue’s monitor or make the queue safe by itself.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.Queue;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentLinkedQueue;
import java.util.concurrent.locks.LockSupport;

public final class LockSupportHelper {

    private final Queue<Thread> waiting = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>();

    public void registerCurrentThread() {
        waiting.add(Thread.currentThread());
    }

    public void parkCurrentThread() {
        LockSupport.park();
        waiting.remove(Thread.currentThread());
    }

    public void unpark() {
        final Thread thread = waiting.poll();
        if (thread != null) {
            LockSupport.unpark(thread);
        }
    }
}
```

The second queue uses that helper with the same condition-check and registration
protocol. The benefit shown is source structure, not a performance or
correctness improvement.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.Queue;

import static demo.utils.Logs.log;
import static demo.utils.Numbers.requireGreaterThanZero;

public final class SharedQueueUsingHelper {

    private final Queue<Integer> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    private final int capacity;

    /* Thread-safe queues for tracking blocked threads */
    private final LockSupportHelper waitingProducers = new LockSupportHelper();
    private final LockSupportHelper waitingConsumers = new LockSupportHelper();

    public SharedQueueUsingHelper(final int capacity) {
        this.capacity = requireGreaterThanZero(capacity);
    }

    public void produce(final int value) {
        while (true) {
            synchronized (this) {
                /* These two operations (`queue.size() < capacity` and `queue.offer(value)`) need to be done
                    atomically, otherwise there may be a race condition and two or more threads may be able to add
                    elements together, exceeding the queue capacity. */
                if (queue.size() < capacity) {
                    queue.offer(value);
                    log("Produced: " + value + " (size: " + queue.size() + ')');
                    waitingConsumers.unpark();
                    return;
                }

                /* Register while holding the queue lock, then park after releasing it. */
                waitingProducers.registerCurrentThread();
            }

            log("Queue is full. Producer is waiting...");
            waitingProducers.parkCurrentThread(); /* Wait until space is available */
        }
    }

    public int consume() {
        while (true) {
            synchronized (this) {
                /* These two operations (`queue.isEmpty()` and `queue.poll()`) need to be done atomically, otherwise
                    there may be a race condition and two or more threads may be able to poll elements at the same
                    time, even when there are no more elements available.*/
                if (!queue.isEmpty()) {
                    final int value = queue.poll();
                    log("Consumed: " + value + " (size: " + queue.size() + ')');
                    waitingProducers.unpark();
                    return value;
                }

                /* Register while holding the queue lock, then park after releasing it. */
                waitingConsumers.registerCurrentThread();
            }

            log("Queue is empty. Consumer is waiting...");
            waitingConsumers.parkCurrentThread(); /* Wait until an item is available */
        }
    }

    public int capacity() {
        return capacity;
    }

    public boolean isEmpty() {
        return queue.isEmpty();
    }
}
```

The runnable example executes both versions in separate, labelled rounds. A
producer supplies values and an end marker; a consumer reads until that marker.
Both tasks are joined before the next round.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;
import java.util.function.IntConsumer;
import java.util.function.IntSupplier;
import java.util.stream.IntStream;

import static demo.utils.Logs.*;
import static demo.utils.Threads.sleepForAFewMilliseconds;

public final class Main {

    public static void main(final String[] args) {
        logHeaderAndJavaVersion("Lock Support");

        final SharedQueue queue = new SharedQueue(5);
        runExample("Shared queue without a helper", queue::produce, queue::consume);

        final SharedQueueUsingHelper queueUsingHelper = new SharedQueueUsingHelper(5);
        runExample("Shared queue using LockSupportHelper", queueUsingHelper::produce, queueUsingHelper::consume);

        log("Completed");
    }

    private static void runExample(final String title, final IntConsumer produce, final IntSupplier consume) {
        logSection(title);
        log("Create Producer");
        final CompletableFuture<Void> producer = CompletableFuture.runAsync(() ->
                IntStream.concat(IntStream.rangeClosed(1, 10), IntStream.of(NO_MORE_ENTRIES) /* Used to signal to the consumer that there are not more elements */)
                        .peek(i -> {if (i > 6) {sleepForAFewMilliseconds();}})
                        .forEach(produce));

        log("Create Consumer");
        final CompletableFuture<Void> consumer = CompletableFuture.runAsync(() -> {
            /* Keep reading from the queue until the NO_MORE_ENTRIES is read */
            for (int i; (i = consume.getAsInt()) != NO_MORE_ENTRIES; ) {
                log("Consumed " + i + " from the queue");
            }
        });

        producer.join();
        consumer.join();
    }

    private static final int NO_MORE_ENTRIES = -1;
}
```

messages, timestamps, and interleavings depend on scheduling and do not prove a
happens-before relationship. A waiting message does not prove the thread
actually blocked; its permit may already be available.
